title: Finite pushforward preserves constructibility on Noetherian schemes
statement:
Let $U$ be Noetherian, let $h:V\to U$ be finite, and let $E$ be a
constructible abelian etale sheaf on $V$. Then its direct image $h_*E$ is
constructible on $U$.

proof.text: For every closed subset $T\subset U$, give $T$ its reduced scheme structure and put $V_T=V\times_UT$. By the constructible-pullback statement, the pullback of $E$ to $V_T$ (and to any open of $V_T$) is constructible; that statement uses stratifications without the constructible-subset condition of the definition used here, but all schemes involved are Noetherian ($V$ is finite over the Noetherian $U$), where every locally closed subset is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset, Stacks 005L], so the two notions agree. The finite-exchange statement identifies $(h_*E)|_T$ with the direct image of this constructible pullback along the finite map $V_T\to T$.

We prove that $(h_*E)|_T$ has a finite lisse partition by Noetherian induction on these closed subsets. The empty subset is immediate. If $T$ is reducible, the finite-components statement gives finitely many irreducible components $T_1,\ldots,T_r$, each a proper closed subset. Apply induction to each and restrict its partition to $T_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}T_j$. These restricted pieces are locally closed, disjoint and cover $T$.

If $T$ is irreducible, its reduced structure is integral. Choose a nonempty affine open $Q\subset T$ and apply the generic finite-pushforward statement to $V_Q\to Q$. It supplies a dense open $Q^\circ\subset T$ on which $(h_*E)|_T$ is lisse. The proper closed complement $T\setminus Q^\circ$ has a finite lisse partition by induction. Adjoining $Q^\circ$ gives the required partition of $T$. At $T=U_{\mathrm{red}}$, its locally closed pieces, composed with $U_{\mathrm{red}}\to U$, are locally closed subschemes partitioning $U$, and each piece is a constructible subset because $U$ is Noetherian [def-weil-constructible-subset, Stacks 005L], which proves constructibility on $U$. No finite bound on the Krull dimension is used.
